one_line_thesis: Turnaround beverage contract manufacturer: FY2025 revenue $1.19B, operating inflection Q1 2026, but negative owner cash and ~$375M debt cap returns; Forward IRR unavailable; dated cash flows and publication checks required.

deep_dive.executive_summary:
Westrock Coffee is a turnaround beverage contract manufacturer scaling through liquid extracts, ready-to-drink formats, and its Conway, Arkansas production hub. FY2025 revenue was $1.19 billion (+40%); Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA $69.7 million; net loss $90.4 million; long-term debt $360.7 million. Q1 2026 inflected with revenue $308.8 million (+44% year over year) and operating income $3.2 million, though net loss remained $8.5 million and stockholders equity was negative $20.2 million.

At $7.04 per share, we expect about -6.37% per year over seven years on normalized owner cash of $0.15...

FY2025 10-K: revenue $1.19B (+40%); Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA $69.7M; net loss $90.4M; negative equity
Warrant exchange offer completed; no outstanding public warrants at year-end 2025
FY2024 10-K filed; Conway facility scale-up costs elevated; secured leverage covenant amendments in effect
Follow-on equity offering (424B5) at $9.88/share to fund growth capex
S-3 shelf registration filed for future equity/debt issuance flexibility
Public listing via SPAC merger (Riverview Acquisition Corp.); Nasdaq ticker WEST
Conway, Arkansas extract and ready-to-drink facility investment program begins (multi-year capex cycle)
Founder-led private company growth phase; pre-IPO revenue scale ~$700M+ run-rate

industry.structure: Fragmented contract roasting and beverage-ingredient market with large foodservice and private-label buyers; Westrock positions as a brand-behind-the-brand solutions partner rather than a consumer brand.
industry.share_shift: Liquid extracts, cold brew, and ready-to-drink formats are gaining mix versus traditional hot-brew bags; Westrock revenue growth (+40% FY2025) suggests share gains in away-from-home channels.
industry.trend: Elevated green-coffee commodity prices, tariff uncertainty on imported equipment, and sustainability/traceability demands are raising working-capital needs and favor vertically integrated suppliers with SS&T capabilities.
